# denote

Portal and facade for audio-to-symbol tools (MIDI, chords, pitch from audio).

Denote wraps multiple audio analysis backends behind a unified Python interface.
Each backend is an optional dependency — install only what you need.

## Install

```bash
pip install denote                          # core only (librosa)
pip install denote[basic_pitch]             # + MIDI transcription
pip install denote[torchcrepe]              # + GPU pitch estimation
pip install denote[all]                     # everything
```

## Quick Start

```python
import denote

# Audio to MIDI (requires basic-pitch)
result = denote.transcribe("song.wav")
result.midi  # pretty_midi.PrettyMIDI object
result.notes  # list of NoteEvent(start_time, end_time, pitch, velocity)

# Pitch estimation (requires torchcrepe, or falls back to librosa pYIN)
pitch = denote.get_pitch("vocal.wav")
pitch.times  # timestamps in seconds
pitch.frequencies  # Hz (NaN for unvoiced)
pitch.confidence  # voicing confidence

# Beat tracking (uses librosa, no extra install needed)
beats = denote.get_beats("song.wav")
beats.beats  # beat times in seconds
beats.tempo  # BPM estimate

# Source separation (requires torch + torchaudio; weights download once)
stems = denote.separate("song.wav")
stems.stems  # {"drums", "bass", "other", "vocals"}: (2, frames) at stems.sr (44.1 kHz)
stems.vocals  # the voice, mono

# Key estimation (uses librosa, no extra install needed)
key = denote.get_key("song.wav")
key.key  # "A minor"
key.confidence  # the winner's profile correlation (not a probability)
key.margin  # lead over the runner-up: small means ambiguous
key.ranked[:3]  # all 24 keys, best first; key.relative names the relative key
```

## Choose Your Backend

```python
# See what's available
denote.list_backends()  # all registered backends
denote.list_backends("pitch")  # ['librosa_pyin', 'pesto', 'swift_f0', 'torchcrepe']

# Each backend's tasks, code licence, weights licence and commercial use
# of the outputs ('yes', 'no', 'conditional', 'unclear' or 'provider terms'), read from
# configs: nothing is loaded
denote.backend_table("pitch")

# Specify a backend explicitly
pitch = denote.get_pitch("vocal.wav", backend="librosa_pyin")
```

## Service-Level Access

For more control, access backends via the service layer:

```python
# Per-backend service handle
denote.services.basic_pitch.transcribe("song.wav", onset_threshold=0.3)
denote.services.torchcrepe.get_pitch("vocal.wav", model="tiny", device="cuda")

# Native adapter (full backend API)
denote.services.basic_pitch.adapter
```

## Supported Backends

| Backend                                   | Task                              | Code licence   | Weights licence (commercial use)                                             | Install                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Basic Pitch (Spotify)                     | MIDI transcription                | Apache 2.0     | Apache 2.0 (yes)                                                             | `pip install denote[basic_pitch]`                             |
| torchcrepe                                | Pitch estimation                  | MIT            | MIT (yes)                                                                    | `pip install denote[torchcrepe]`                              |
| SwiftF0                                   | Pitch estimation                  | MIT            | MIT (yes)                                                                    | `pip install denote[swift_f0]`                                |
| PESTO                                     | Pitch estimation                  | LGPL 3.0       | LGPL 3.0 (yes; redistributing the weights carries LGPL terms)                | `pip install denote[pesto]`                                   |
| librosa pYIN                              | Pitch estimation                  | ISC            | no weights (yes)                                                             | (included)                                                    |
| Beat This!                                | Beats + downbeats                 | MIT            | MIT (yes)                                                                    | `pip install denote[beat_this]`                               |
| librosa beats                             | Beat tracking                     | ISC            | no weights (yes)                                                             | (included)                                                    |
| librosa key (Krumhansl-Schmuckler)        | Key estimation                    | ISC            | no weights (yes)                                                             | (included)                                                    |
| Hybrid Demucs (torchaudio)                | Source separation                 | BSD 2-Clause   | unstated; author says research use (unclear)                                 | `pip install denote[torchaudio_hdemucs]`                      |
| HTDemucs on MLX (`demucs_mlx`)            | Source separation (Apple silicon) | MIT            | unstated; converted from the same Demucs checkpoints (unclear)               | own environment: `python -m denote.isolated build demucs_mlx` |
| RoFormer via audio-separator (`roformer`) | Source separation                 | MIT            | default checkpoint MIT (yes); other community checkpoints unstated (unclear) | own environment: `python -m denote.isolated build roformer`   |

`denote.backend_table()` gives the same columns from the backends’ configs, where each licence’s source is cited.

More backends coming: madmom, autochord.

### Backends in their own environment

Some models pin dependencies that cannot share denote’s environment (`demucs-mlx` pins its MLX, `audio-separator` needs torch>=2.13 on Apple silicon). Those backends run their model in a separate Python environment that denote builds with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) from pinned requirements (through [`ps.isolated`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ps)), and talk to it through a long-lived worker process, so the model loads once:

```bash
python -m denote.isolated build demucs_mlx   # one-time
python -m denote.isolated status             # which are built, and where
```

```python
result = denote.separate("song.wav", backend="demucs_mlx")  # htdemucs on MLX
result.stems  # {"drums", "bass", "other", "vocals"}
vocals = denote.separate("song.wav", backend="roformer").vocals  # Mel-Band RoFormer
denote.services["roformer"].close()  # free the worker's memory
```

Environments live in `~/.local/share/denote/envs/<backend>` (set `DENOTE_DATA_DIR` to move them). A missing one raises `denote.isolated.EnvNotBuilt` with the build command; pass `build_env=True` to build it on first use instead. Building needs `uv` on the `PATH`. Each environment is installed from a lock kept with its backend (`env.lock`, every package pinned), so it is reproducible; `python -m denote.isolated lock <backend>` re-resolves it. A backend’s worker keeps its model loaded (4.5 to 6 GB for these two) until `denote.services[<backend>].close()` or the end of the process.

## Plugin System

Register your own backends:

```python
import denote

denote.register_backend(
    "my_tool",
    config={
        "name": "my_tool",
        "tasks": ["transcribe"],
        "pip_install": "my-tool",
    },
    adapter=MyAdapter(config),
)
```

# _autosummary/denote.align.html.md

# denote.align

Align a symbolic score to a recording of the same music (audio-to-score sync).

[`align_score()`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.align_score) answers “which moment of the score is playing at time *t*
of this recording?” (and the reverse), for a score and a performance that
differ in tempo, rubato, intro length, even key. It is the bridge you need to
cut a score and a recording at the same musical point, to compare several
scores of a piece against one recording, or to put score positions on a
recording’s timeline.

Method: chroma features on both sides (the score’s piano roll folded to pitch
classes, no synthesis needed; the audio’s constant-Q chroma), cosine distance,
and dynamic time warping (`librosa.sequence.dtw`). By default the recording
is matched as a *subsequence* of the score, so a clip of the first minute finds
its place inside a full-length score. `transpose="auto"` also tries all
twelve transpositions of the score and keeps the best, because arrangements
are often in another key.

The result’s `cost` (mean cosine distance along the path, 0 = identical
pitch content, 1 = unrelated) is comparable across scores aligned to the same
recording, which makes it a ranking of how faithful each score is.

| [`DFLT_FRAME_RATE`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.DFLT_FRAME_RATE)   | Default analysis rate (frames per second) for both score and audio.   |

| [`N_PITCH_CLASSES`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.N_PITCH_CLASSES)   | Pitch classes per chroma column.                                      |

### denote.align.align_audio(audio, reference, , sr=None, reference_sr=None, subsequence=False, transpose=0, frame_rate=10.0, audio_sr=22050)

Align two recordings of the same music (a cover, a render, a remix).

The same chroma DTW as [`align_score()`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.align_score), with a recording in the
score’s place: `score_times` are times in `reference`. The `cost` is
a measure of how closely `audio` follows `reference`’s harmony and
melody, tolerant of tempo differences and blind to timbre, which makes it
a fidelity score for generated versions of a piece.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), `ndarray`]) – The recording to place on the reference’s timeline.
  * **reference** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), `ndarray`]) – The reference recording.
  * **sr** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Sample rate when `audio` is an array.
  * **reference_sr** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Sample rate when `reference` is an array.
  * **subsequence** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Match `audio` anywhere inside `reference` (default
    `False`: both start and end together).
  * **transpose** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Semitones, or `"auto"` to try all twelve.
  * **frame_rate** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Analysis frames per second.
  * **audio_sr** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Rate both are resampled to before analysis.
* **Return type:**
  [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment)
* **Returns:**
  A [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment) (`score_*` refers to `reference`).

### denote.align.align_chroma(query, reference, , subsequence=True, transpose=0, frame_rate=10.0, steps=array([[1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 1]]), silent='uniform')

Align two precomputed pitch-class feature sequences (rows x frames).

The DTW behind [`align_score()`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.align_score) and [`align_audio()`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.align_audio), for callers
with their own features: a band-limited chroma, a chroma with a drone’s
steady background removed, a symbolic chroma at another resolution. Both
must have the same rows and be at `frame_rate` frames per second.

* **Parameters:**
  * **query** (`ndarray`) – The sequence to place (`query_times` / `audio_times`).
  * **reference** (`ndarray`) – The sequence it is placed on (`reference_times` /
    `score_times`).
  * **subsequence** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Match the shorter of the two anywhere inside the longer
    (default), else both start and end together.
  * **transpose** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Semitones to roll the reference’s pitch classes, or
    `"auto"` to try all twelve and keep the lowest-cost one (12-row
    chroma only).
  * **frame_rate** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Frames per second of both, to turn frames into seconds.
  * **steps** (`ndarray`) – DTW step sizes as (query frames, reference frames) rows. The
    default bounds the tempo ratio to half or double.
  * **silent** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How a silent (zero) column counts: `"uniform"` (the flat
    chroma, the default) or `"zero"` (similar to nothing).
* **Return type:**
  [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment)
* **Returns:**
  A [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment); its `cost` is the mean cosine distance
  along the path (0 = same pitch content), its `raw["path"]` the
  (query, reference) frame pairs.

Example:

```default
a = denote.align_chroma(take_chroma, seed_chroma, frame_rate=10)
1 - a.cost  # mean cosine similarity along the alignment
```

### denote.align.align_score(score, audio, , sr=None, subsequence=True, transpose=0, frame_rate=10.0, audio_sr=22050)

Align a score to a recording of (part of) the same music.

* **Parameters:**
  * **score** – A `pretty_midi.PrettyMIDI` or a `.mid` path (other score
    formats when `audiate` is installed).
  * **audio** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), `ndarray`]) – A recording: a path, or an array with `sr`.
  * **sr** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Sample rate when `audio` is an array.
  * **subsequence** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Match the recording anywhere inside the score (default),
    e.g. a one-minute clip against a full score. `False` forces the
    two to start and end together.
  * **transpose** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Semitones to shift the score’s pitch classes, or `"auto"`
    to try all twelve and keep the lowest-cost one.
  * **frame_rate** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Analysis frames per second for both sides.
  * **audio_sr** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Rate the audio is resampled to before analysis.
* **Return type:**
  [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment)
* **Returns:**
  A [`ScoreAlignment`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.ScoreAlignment).

Example:

```default
a = denote.align_score("theme.mid", "recording_first_minute.wav")
a.audio_to_score(60.0)      # where the score is when the clip ends
a.cost                      # compare scores of the same piece
```

# _autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md

# denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat

Make basic-pitch importable and runnable against today’s dependencies.

basic-pitch pins old dependencies. On Python 3.12, pip resolves only 0.3.0 on
macOS, and no release at all on Linux (each pins a TensorFlow with no cp312
wheel), so it gets installed with `--no-deps`. Either way it runs against current
scipy, setuptools and stray TensorFlow leftovers. Three things then break (issue #2):

1. `import tensorflow` succeeds on an empty `tensorflow/` namespace folder (left
   by an uninstall), so basic-pitch sets `TF_PRESENT` and later fails on
   `import tensorflow.lite`.
2. resampy < 0.4.3, which basic-pitch pins, imports `pkg_resources`, removed
   from setuptools >= 81.
3. basic-pitch < 0.4 calls `scipy.signal.gaussian`, removed in scipy >= 1.13
   (now `scipy.signal.windows.gaussian`).

Each fix below is applied only when its failure condition holds, and each is scoped
as narrowly as the failure allows. Nothing is patched globally that a working
install would see: a real TensorFlow is left alone, `pkg_resources` is stubbed
only while resampy is imported, and the scipy alias is visible to basic-pitch’s
`note_creation` module only.

Use [`import_basic_pitch()`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.import_basic_pitch) rather than importing `basic_pitch` directly.

### Module Attributes

| [`MODEL_RUNTIMES`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.MODEL_RUNTIMES)     | Model runtimes basic-pitch can use, by import name, and the pip name to suggest.      |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ONNX_MODEL_RELPATH`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.ONNX_MODEL_RELPATH) | The ONNX serialization of the ICASSP 2022 model, relative to the basic_pitch package. |

### Functions

| [`hide_broken_tensorflow`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.hide_broken_tensorflow)()              | Make `import tensorflow` fail if TensorFlow is only an empty folder.                 |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`import_basic_pitch`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.import_basic_pitch)()                  | Import basic-pitch with the fixes above; return `(predict, model_path)`.             |
| [`is_namespace_leftover`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.is_namespace_leftover)(name)           | True if `name` is importable only as an empty namespace package.                     |
| [`model_path`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.model_path)(basic_pitch)               | The model file to load: ONNX when onnxruntime is usable, else basic-pitch's default. |
| [`preload_resampy`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.preload_resampy)()                     | Import resampy even when `pkg_resources` is gone (setuptools >= 81).                 |
| [`restore_scipy_gaussian`](_autosummary/denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.html.md#denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.restore_scipy_gaussian)(note_creation) | Give `note_creation` a `scipy.signal.gaussian` if scipy no longer has one.           |

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.MODEL_RUNTIMES *= {'coremltools': 'coremltools', 'onnxruntime': 'onnxruntime', 'tensorflow': 'tensorflow', 'tflite_runtime': 'tflite-runtime'}*

Model runtimes basic-pitch can use, by import name, and the pip name to suggest.

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.ONNX_MODEL_RELPATH *= PosixPath('saved_models/icassp_2022/nmp.onnx')*

The ONNX serialization of the ICASSP 2022 model, relative to the basic_pitch package.

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.hide_broken_tensorflow()

Make `import tensorflow` fail if TensorFlow is only an empty folder.

basic-pitch decides at import time whether TensorFlow is present from a bare
`import tensorflow`. If the leftover was already imported (say, by an earlier
`import basic_pitch`), it is evicted and basic-pitch’s `TF_PRESENT` reset,
which still takes effect as long as `basic_pitch.inference` is not yet
imported. Returns True if it hid a leftover.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.import_basic_pitch()

Import basic-pitch with the fixes above; return `(predict, model_path)`.

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.is_namespace_leftover(name)

True if `name` is importable only as an empty namespace package.

That is what an uninstall leaves behind when stray files kept the folder: the
import succeeds, but nothing in it works.

```pycon
>>> is_namespace_leftover('json')
False
>>> is_namespace_leftover('surely_not_an_installed_module_xyz')
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.model_path(basic_pitch)

The model file to load: ONNX when onnxruntime is usable, else basic-pitch’s default.

ONNX loads the same everywhere, unlike the TensorFlow SavedModel, whose loader
breaks across TensorFlow versions.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.preload_resampy()

Import resampy even when `pkg_resources` is gone (setuptools >= 81).

resampy < 0.4.3 uses only `pkg_resources.resource_filename`. A stub providing
it is put in `sys.modules` for the duration of resampy’s import and removed
after, so no other library ever sees a partial `pkg_resources`. Returns True
if the stub was needed.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### denote.backends.basic_pitch.compat.restore_scipy_gaussian(note_creation)

Give `note_creation` a `scipy.signal.gaussian` if scipy no longer has one.

Only that module’s `scipy` name is replaced, by a proxy of the real scipy, so
scipy itself is not modified. Returns True if the alias was needed.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

# denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter

Adapter for key estimation from librosa chroma and published key profiles.

### Functions

| [`chroma_cens`](_autosummary/denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.chroma_cens)(y, sr)                       | CENS chromagram: CQT chroma smoothed and quantized, robust to timbre.       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`chroma_stft`](_autosummary/denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.chroma_stft)(y, sr)                       | STFT chromagram: faster than CQT, coarser in the bass.                      |
| [`frame_rms`](_autosummary/denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.frame_rms)(y, n_frames, \*[, hop_length]) | RMS per frame, resampled to `n_frames` (so any chroma callable can use it). |

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.Adapter)(config)   | Key estimation: weighted mean chroma correlated with 24 rotated key profiles.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Key estimation: weighted mean chroma correlated with 24 rotated key profiles.

#### get_key(audio, , sr=None, \*\*kwargs)

Estimate the key (tonic + mode) of a whole recording.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required if audio is an array).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – `profile` (a name in `denote.keys.KEY_PROFILES`, default
    `"krumhansl"`, or a `(major, minor)` pair of 12 weights),
    `chroma` (`"cqt"` default, `"stft"`, `"cens"`, or a callable
    `(y, sr) -> (12, frames)`), `audio_sr` (rate the audio is
    resampled to first, default 22050), `weighting` (`"energy"`
    default: frames weighted by RMS; or `"uniform"`), `min_rms`
    and `min_duration_s` (refuse quieter or shorter audio).
* **Returns:**
  KeyResult; `confidence` is the winning key’s Pearson correlation,
  `margin` its lead over the runner-up, `scores` all 24 keys best
  first, `raw` the averaged chroma, the RMS and the duration.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – audio shorter than `min_duration_s` or quieter than
      `min_rms`, or an unknown `chroma`/`weighting`/`profile`.

### denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.chroma_cens(y, sr)

CENS chromagram: CQT chroma smoothed and quantized, robust to timbre.

### denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.chroma_stft(y, sr)

STFT chromagram: faster than CQT, coarser in the bass.

### denote.backends.librosa_key.adapter.frame_rms(y, n_frames, , hop_length=512)

RMS per frame, resampled to `n_frames` (so any chroma callable can use it).

# _autosummary/denote.backends.pesto.adapter.html.md

# denote.backends.pesto.adapter

Adapter for PESTO — self-supervised pitch estimation (Sony CSL).

### Functions

| [`frame_period`](_autosummary/denote.backends.pesto.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.pesto.adapter.frame_period)(step_size_ms, sr)   | Seconds between PESTO's frames for a `step_size_ms` step at `sr`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/denote.backends.pesto.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.pesto.adapter.Adapter)(config)   | PESTO adapter for monophonic pitch/F0 estimation.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|

### *class* denote.backends.pesto.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

PESTO adapter for monophonic pitch/F0 estimation.

#### get_pitch(audio, , sr=None, \*\*kwargs)

Estimate pitch from audio with PESTO.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path, numpy array or torch tensor.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required if audio is an array).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Normalized parameters: `step_size_ms` (default 10),
    `model` (checkpoint name or path), `reduction`, `device`,
    `confidence_threshold` (default 0.5), `normalize` (default
    True: peak-normalise first, since PESTO’s confidence falls with
    level and no frame is voiced at -30 dBFS; False passes the level
    through).
* **Returns:**
  PitchResult with .times, .frequencies (NaN where unvoiced) and
  .confidence; `.raw` holds the pitch, volume and activations.

### denote.backends.pesto.adapter.frame_period(step_size_ms, sr)

Seconds between PESTO’s frames for a `step_size_ms` step at `sr`.

PESTO rounds the step to whole samples (`int(step * sr / 1000 + 0.5)`), so
the true period is that hop over `sr`, not `step_size_ms / 1000`: at
22050 Hz a 10 ms step is 221 samples (10.023 ms), and times built from the
nominal step drift 0.23 % (0.7 s at 5 minutes).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### *class* denote.backends.swift_f0.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

SwiftF0 adapter for monophonic pitch/F0 estimation.

#### get_pitch(audio, , sr=None, \*\*kwargs)

Estimate pitch from audio with SwiftF0.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path, numpy array or torch tensor.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required if audio is an array).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Normalized parameters: `min_frequency`, `max_frequency`
    (clipped to the model’s 46.875-2093.75 Hz), `confidence_threshold`
    (default 0.5, SwiftF0’s calibrated voicing threshold), `threads`,
    `normalize` (default True: peak-normalise first, since SwiftF0
    calls quiet input unvoiced; frames peaking below 1e-3 are forced
    unvoiced. False passes the level through).
* **Returns:**
  PitchResult with .times, .frequencies (NaN where unvoiced) and
  .confidence; `.raw` is SwiftF0’s own result (with loudness_db).

### denote.backends.swift_f0.adapter.SWIFT_F0_SR *= 16000*

SwiftF0’s model rate; audio is resampled to it here (so no soxr is needed).

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.html.md#denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.Adapter)(config)   | Hybrid Demucs: drums, bass, other, vocals from a stereo mix.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Hybrid Demucs: drums, bass, other, vocals from a stereo mix.

#### separate(audio, , sr=None, \*\*kwargs)

Separate a mix into stems.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path, numpy array or torch tensor (mono, `(frames, channels)`
    or `(channels, frames)`); mono is duplicated to stereo.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required if audio is an array).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Normalized parameters (see `config.param_map`):
    `segment_s` (chunk length; memory per chunk grows with it),
    `overlap_s` (crossfade between chunks, 0 allowed, shorter than
    `segment_s`), `device`, `bundle` (a torchaudio.pipelines name:
    `HDEMUCS_HIGH_MUSDB_PLUS` or `HDEMUCS_HIGH_MUSDB`), `sources`
    (stem names to keep, default all; the others are never stored).
* **Return type:**
  [`SeparationResult`](_autosummary/denote.base.html.md#denote.base.SeparationResult)
* **Returns:**
  SeparationResult with `(2, frames)` stems at the bundle’s rate (44.1 kHz).
  The model’s four stems add up to the mix up to its own error (a few %);
  `.vocals` is mono.

### denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.HDEMUCS_BUNDLES *= ('HDEMUCS_HIGH_MUSDB_PLUS', 'HDEMUCS_HIGH_MUSDB')*

The torchaudio.pipelines bundles this adapter runs (four-stem Hybrid Demucs).

### denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.MIN_FRAMES *= 1281*

Shortest input HDemucs accepts for sure. Measured on the torchaudio bundles
(nfft 4096, hop 1024): lengths 769..1024 and >= 1281 run, 1..768 and 1025..1280
fail inside `_spec` (“Spectrogram’s last dimension must be …”), because its
reflect padding falls back to extra zero padding that changes the frame count.
Shorter chunks are zero-padded to this and cropped back.

### denote.backends.torchaudio_hdemucs.adapter.NORM_EPS *= 1e-08*

Added to the mix’s std before normalizing, so silence does not divide by zero.

Estimate pitch from audio using CREPE.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required if audio is an array).

### denote.backends.torchcrepe.adapter.CREPE_SR *= 16000*

it resamples every input to it.

* **Type:**
  torchcrepe’s model rate

### denote.backends.torchcrepe.adapter.frame_period(hop_length, sr)

Seconds between torchcrepe’s frames for `hop_length` samples at `sr`.

torchcrepe resamples to 16 kHz and truncates the hop there
(`int(hop * 16000 / sr)`), so the frame period is that over 16000, not
`hop / sr`: at 22050 Hz a 220-sample hop is really 219.12 samples, and
times built from `hop / sr` drift 0.4 % (1.2 s at 5 minutes).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### denote.base.COMMERCIAL_USE_VALUES *= ('yes', 'no', 'conditional', 'unclear', 'provider terms')*

What a backend’s `commercial_use` config field may say, about using its
OUTPUTS (what the model produces) commercially: the terms allow it (`"yes"`),
forbid it (`"no"`), allow it under conditions such as a revenue cap or a use
restriction (`"conditional"`), the terms are not settled: the licence is
unstated, disputed or withdrawn, or the training-data chain is doubtful
(“unclear”), or the weights are not public and a hosted service’s own terms
decide (`"provider terms"`, kept for a future hosted backend). The field is
about using outputs commercially; obligations on redistributing the weights
themselves (LGPL and the like) belong in `weights_license` (with prose in
`weights_license_note`). The same tuple as arioso’s.

### *class* denote.base.ChordResult(intervals, labels=list(), raw=None, backend='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Result of chord recognition.

### *class* denote.base.KeyResult(key, tonic, mode, confidence, margin=0.0, scores=dict(), profile='', raw=None, backend='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Result of key estimation: tonic + mode, with every candidate key’s score.

`confidence` is the winning key’s score: for profile backends (`librosa_key`)
the Pearson correlation, in [-1, 1], between the recording’s mean chroma and that
key’s profile. It measures fit, and is not a probability. `margin` is the
winner’s score minus the runner-up’s; a small margin means two keys fit about
equally well, most often the relative key (C major / A minor share every pitch
class), the parallel key or a key a fifth away. Look at `ranked` before
trusting the winner when the margin is small.

#### *property* ranked *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]*

`[(key, score), ...]` for every candidate key, best first (`scores`’ order).

#### *property* relative *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The relative key of the estimate (C major -> A minor); `""` if none applies.

Only major and minor have a relative key here; a backend reporting another
mode (dorian, …) gets `""`.

#### *property* runner_up *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The second-best key (`""` when only one was scored).

# _autosummary/denote.compare.html.md

# denote.compare

Compare a version of a piece with a reference: harmony and sound, on the same moments (denote#3).

[`align_audio()`](_autosummary/denote.align.html.md#denote.align.align_audio) measures how closely a version follows the
reference’s harmony and melody (chroma DTW), and is blind to timbre on purpose.
[`compare_audio()`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.compare_audio) adds the other half, how close the *sound* is, and keeps
both on one footing: the two recordings are aligned once, and every metric reads
the same warping path, so each compares the same musical moments.

Metrics are a registry ([`METRICS`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.METRICS), a `name -> metric` mapping you can
extend or replace through `metrics=`): a metric is a callable taking an
[`AlignedPair`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.AlignedPair) and returning a distance (lower is closer). An embedding
metric (CLAP, MERT, a Fréchet-style distance) is one more entry, with no change
to callers.

Built in:

- `"chroma"`: the alignment’s own cost, mean cosine distance between chroma
  frames along the path (0 identical pitch content, 1 unrelated). Measured on an
  orchestral minute, an unrelated piece in the same key and style scored about
  0.16-0.21 against the reference, so it discriminates mainly below about 0.15.
- `"timbre"`: MFCCs `c1..c19` (`c0`, loudness, left out) of both
  recordings, each coefficient z-scored with statistics pooled over both (so a
  global difference in spectral shape is kept, not normalised away), then the
  root-mean-square difference per coefficient, averaged along the path. 0 is the
  same sound; two unrelated timbres are typically around 1. The starter it
  replaces (z-scored per recording) separated a General MIDI render
  (0.46-0.79) from a light audio-to-audio pass of the original (0.41); it is a
  coarse spectral-envelope measure, not a perceptual one.

### Module Attributes

| [`Metric`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.Metric)       | an aligned pair -> a distance (lower is closer).                                                            |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`METRICS`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.METRICS)      | The built-in metrics, by name.                                                                              |
| [`DFLT_METRICS`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.DFLT_METRICS) | What [`compare_audio()`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.compare_audio) computes when `metrics` is not given. |

### Functions

| [`compare_audio`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.compare_audio)(audio, reference, \*[, ...])   | How close `audio` is to `reference`, metric by metric, on the same musical moments.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`chroma_metric`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.chroma_metric)(pair)                          | The alignment's chroma cost: mean cosine distance along the path.                     |
| [`timbre_metric`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.timbre_metric)(pair, \*[, n_mfcc])            | Mean RMS difference of pooled-z-scored MFCCs `c1..` along the path; see the module.   |

### Classes

| [`AlignedPair`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.AlignedPair)(audio, reference, sr, ...)   | Two recordings at one rate, and the alignment between them, as metrics see them.    |

  [`AudioComparison`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.AudioComparison)
* **Returns:**
  An [`AudioComparison`](_autosummary/denote.compare.html.md#denote.compare.AudioComparison).

Example:

```default
c = denote.compare_audio("render.wav", "original.wav")
c["chroma"], c["timbre"]
```

Mean RMS difference of pooled-z-scored MFCCs `c1..` along the path; see the module.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/denote.html.md

# denote

Denote — Portal and facade for audio-to-symbol tools.

Simple usage:

```default
import denote
result = denote.transcribe("song.wav")         # audio -> MIDI
chords = denote.get_chords("song.wav")         # audio -> chord labels
pitch = denote.get_pitch("vocal.wav")           # audio -> F0
beats = denote.get_beats("song.wav")            # audio -> beat times
key = denote.get_key("song.wav")                # audio -> "A minor" + scores
sync = denote.align_score("song.mid", "song.wav")  # score <-> recording time map

denote.list_backends()                          # see what's available
denote.list_backends('pitch')                   # backends for a task
denote.backend_table()                          # tasks + weights licence per backend
```

Service-level access:

```default
denote.services.basic_pitch.transcribe("song.wav", onset_threshold=0.3)
denote.services.torchcrepe.get_pitch("vocal.wav", model='tiny')
```

Native adapter access:

```default
denote.services.basic_pitch.adapter  # raw adapter instance
```

### Module Attributes

| [`BACKEND_TABLE_FIELDS`](_autosummary/denote.html.md#denote.BACKEND_TABLE_FIELDS)   | The config fields [`backend_table()`](_autosummary/denote.html.md#denote.backend_table) reports, in column order.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`get_key`](_autosummary/denote.html.md#denote.get_key)(audio, \*[, sr, backend])    | Estimate the key (tonic + mode) of a recording.                                     |
| [`get_pitch`](_autosummary/denote.html.md#denote.get_pitch)(audio, \*[, sr, backend])  | Estimate pitch/F0 from audio.                                                       |
| [`separate`](_autosummary/denote.html.md#denote.separate)(audio, \*[, sr, backend])   | Separate a mix into stems (drums, bass, other, vocals, ...).                        |

### denote.backend_table(task=None, , fields=('name', 'tasks', 'license', 'weights_license', 'commercial_use'))

One row per backend: its tasks, code licence, weights licence and commercial use.

Reads the backends’ configs only, so no adapter (and no optional dependency)
is loaded. `commercial_use` is one of `COMMERCIAL_USE_VALUES`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **task** – If set, only backends for this task (‘pitch’, ‘beats’, …).
  * **fields** – The config keys each row carries (a missing key reads `None`).
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)
* **Returns:**
  A list of dicts, one per backend (sorted by name), keyed by `fields`.

Example:

```default
free = [r["name"] for r in denote.backend_table("pitch") if r["commercial_use"] == "yes"]
```

### denote.get_beats(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Track beats in audio.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name. Defaults to ‘librosa_beats’.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters (hop_length, start_bpm).
* **Returns:**
  BeatResult with .beats, .downbeats, .tempo fields.

### denote.get_chords(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Recognize chords from audio.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters.
* **Returns:**
  ChordResult with .intervals, .labels fields.

### denote.get_key(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Estimate the key (tonic + mode) of a recording.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name. Defaults to ‘librosa_key’.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters (`profile`: ‘krumhansl’ default or
    ‘temperley’ or a (major, minor) pair; `chroma`: ‘cqt’ default,
    ‘stft’, ‘cens’ or a callable (y, sr) -> (12, frames)).
* **Returns:**
  KeyResult with .key (“A minor”), .tonic, .mode, .confidence (the winner’s
  profile correlation, not a probability), .margin (lead over the runner-up),
  .scores (all 24 keys, best first) and .relative.

Example:

```default
k = denote.get_key("song.wav")
k.key, k.margin, k.ranked[:2]
```

### denote.get_pitch(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Estimate pitch/F0 from audio.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name. Defaults to ‘torchcrepe’ if installed,
    falls back to ‘librosa_pyin’.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters (min_frequency, max_frequency,
    model, device, hop_length).
* **Returns:**
  PitchResult with .times, .frequencies, .confidence fields.

### denote.separate(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Separate a mix into stems (drums, bass, other, vocals, …).

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name. Defaults to ‘torchaudio_hdemucs’. ‘demucs_mlx’ and
    ‘roformer’ run in their own environment (see `denote.isolated`).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters. All take `sources` (stem names
    to keep, in that order). torchaudio_hdemucs: segment_s, overlap_s,
    device, bundle. demucs_mlx: model (‘htdemucs’, ‘htdemucs_ft’,
    ‘htdemucs_6s’), shifts, overlap, seed, build_env. roformer: model (a
    checkpoint file name), build_env. `build_env=True` builds a missing
    environment instead of raising `denote.isolated.EnvNotBuilt`; the
    worker then keeps the model in memory until
    `denote.services[backend].close()` or exit.
* **Returns:**
  (channels, frames)}), .sr, and
  .vocals (mono).
* **Return type:**
  SeparationResult with .stems ({name

Example:

```default
voice = denote.separate("song.mp3").vocals
```

### denote.transcribe(audio, , sr=None, backend=None, \*\*kwargs)

Transcribe audio to MIDI.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – File path (str/Path) or numpy array.
  * **sr** – Sample rate (required when audio is an array).
  * **backend** – Backend name. Defaults to ‘basic_pitch’ if installed.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific parameters (onset_threshold, min_note_length, etc.)
* **Returns:**
  TranscriptionResult with .midi, .notes, and .raw fields.

# _autosummary/denote.isolated.html.md

# denote.isolated

Backends that run in their own Python environment, through `ps.isolated`.

Some models cannot share an environment with denote (or with each other):
`demucs-mlx` pins its own MLX, `audio-separator` needs a recent torch. Their
backends declare an `isolated_env` in `BACKEND_CONFIG` (top-level requirements, a
lock file resolved from them, and the Python version) and keep the model code in a
**worker file**
(`denote/workers/<backend>_worker.py`): a plain module, importing nothing from
denote, that `ps.isolated.Worker` runs with the environment’s interpreter. Requests
and replies are JSON lines; audio crosses as `.npy` files in a temporary folder.

Where things live (`DENOTE_DATA_DIR` replaces the root):

```default
~/.local/share/denote/
    envs/<backend>/      the backend's environment (built by uv)
    models/<backend>/    weights a backend keeps itself (when its library has no
                         cache of its own outside a temporary folder)
```

Nothing is built implicitly: a missing environment raises [`EnvNotBuilt`](_autosummary/denote.isolated.html.md#denote.isolated.EnvNotBuilt), whose
message is the command that builds it (`python -m denote.isolated build <backend>`),
unless the caller passes `build_env=True`.

An environment is installed from its backend’s **lock** (`env.lock` next to its
config: every package pinned, with platform markers, as `uv pip compile --universal`
resolves the top-level requirements), so it is the same wherever and whenever it is
built, and changing the lock changes the spec’s digest (the next build starts afresh).
`python -m denote.isolated lock <backend>` re-resolves it.

A worker keeps its model in memory (several GB for these models) until it is closed
(`denote.services[<backend>].close()`) or the host process exits.

```pycon
>>> spec = env_spec({"name": "toy", "isolated_env": {"requirements": ["numpy==2.1.0"]}})
>>> spec.name, spec.requirements
('toy', ('numpy==2.1.0',))
>>> build_command("toy")
'python -m denote.isolated build toy'
```

# _autosummary/denote.keys.html.md

# denote.keys

Key estimation from pitch-class profiles (the Krumhansl-Schmuckler method).

Correlate a 12-bin pitch-class vector (the mean chroma of a recording, or a note
histogram of a score) with a major and a minor *key profile* rotated to each of the
12 tonics. The best of the 24 Pearson correlations names the key. This module is the
audio-free core; `denote.get_key` computes the chroma and calls it.

```pycon
>>> major = KEY_PROFILES["krumhansl"].major
>>> r = key_from_chroma(major)  # the C major profile itself
>>> r.key, round(r.confidence, 3)
('C major', 1.0)
>>> r.relative
'A minor'
>>> key_from_chroma(np.roll(major, 3)).key  # rotated up three semitones
'Eb major'
>>> parse_key("F# minor")
(6, 'minor')
```

Profiles (`KEY_PROFILES`), each a published table of how well each pitch class
fits a key, tonic first:

- `"krumhansl"`: Krumhansl and Kessler’s probe-tone ratings (Krumhansl & Kessler
  1982; Krumhansl, *Cognitive Foundations of Musical Pitch*, 1990, Table 2.1).
- `"temperley"`: Temperley’s profiles from the Kostka-Payne corpus (Temperley,
  *Music and Probability*, 2007), as listed by Humdrum `keycor`.

Both sets of numbers are as given at [https://extras.humdrum.org/man/keycor/](https://extras.humdrum.org/man/keycor/) (and in
music21’s `analysis.discrete`). Any other `(major, minor)` pair of 12 numbers
can be passed as `profile`.

Key names follow the fewest-accidentals convention (Eb major, C# minor, Gb major,
Eb minor), the one `chordsym` uses for chord spelling.

### Module Attributes

| [`FLAT_RTOL`](_autosummary/denote.keys.html.md#denote.keys.FLAT_RTOL)   | A vector whose spread is below this fraction of its largest value is flat.   |

### Functions

| [`key_from_chroma`](_autosummary/denote.keys.html.md#denote.keys.key_from_chroma)(chroma, \*[, profile, ...])   | The best of the 24 keys for a chroma vector or chromagram.                    |

### denote.keys.key_from_chroma(chroma, , profile='krumhansl', weights=None, backend='')

The best of the 24 keys for a chroma vector or chromagram.

* **Parameters:**
  * **chroma** – `(12,)` pitch-class weights (C first) or a `(12, frames)`
    chromagram, averaged over frames.
  * **profile** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`KeyProfile`](_autosummary/denote.keys.html.md#denote.keys.KeyProfile), [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]]) – A name in `KEY_PROFILES` (default `"krumhansl"`), a
    `KeyProfile`, or a `(major, minor)` pair of 12 weights each.
  * **weights** – Optional per-frame weights for the average (e.g. frame RMS).
  * **backend** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Recorded on the result.
* **Return type:**
  [`KeyResult`](_autosummary/denote.base.html.md#denote.base.KeyResult)
* **Returns:**
  KeyResult whose `confidence` is the winner’s correlation, `margin` the
  gap to the runner-up, `scores` every key’s correlation (best first), and
  `raw["chroma"]` the 12-bin vector correlated.

### denote.keys.key_name(tonic_pc, mode)

`"Eb major"`: the key on pitch class `tonic_pc` (C = 0) in `mode`.

```pycon
>>> key_name(3, "major"), key_name(1, "minor")
('Eb major', 'C# minor')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### denote.keys.key_scores(chroma, , profile='krumhansl')

`{key name: Pearson correlation}` for all 24 keys, best first.

Raises `ValueError` when the vector is flat to within `FLAT_RTOL` (silence,
or no pitched content), since a correlation with a constant is undefined.
Level gating (very quiet or very short audio) is the audio adapter’s job:
per-frame chroma normalization makes even faint noise look pitched here.

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### denote.keys.parse_key(name)

`(tonic_pc, mode)` from a key name.

Accepted: `"Eb major"`, `"c# minor"`, `"A min"`, `"Am"`, `"Amin"`,
`"Amaj"` and a bare uppercase tonic (`"Bb"`, major). A bare *lowercase*
tonic (`"a"`) is rejected, because some conventions read it as minor; say
`"a minor"` or `"am"`.

```pycon
>>> parse_key("Eb major"), parse_key("Am"), parse_key("Bbmaj")
((3, 'major'), (9, 'minor'), (10, 'major'))
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### denote.keys.pitch_class_vector(chroma, , weights=None)

A `(12,)` vector: `chroma` itself, or its mean over frames if `(12, frames)`.

`weights` (one non-negative number per frame) makes it a weighted mean, e.g.
by frame energy so quiet frames count less.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

The key sharing `name`’s key signature: C major <-> A minor.

```pycon
>>> relative_key("C major"), relative_key("F# minor")
('A minor', 'A major')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### denote.util.DFLT_AUDIO_SR *= 22050*

Sample rate audio is resampled to before chroma extraction. librosa’s CQT chroma
needs more than about 8.2 kHz (its top wavelets exceed Nyquist below that), so
every chroma path in denote (align, compare, get_key) loads at this rate.

### denote.util.DFLT_CHROMA_HOP *= 512*

Hop between chroma frames, in samples (librosa’s default).

### denote.util.channels_first(y)

A multichannel array as `(channels, frames)`, whichever way it came.

librosa and torchaudio give `(channels, frames)`, soundfile
`(frames, channels)`. Leading size-1 axes (a batch of one) are dropped. An
axis of size 2 or less beside a longer one is the channels axis, so a
one-frame stereo clip stays stereo; otherwise the longer axis is time.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### denote.util.chunk_bounds(n, , segment, overlap)

`(start, end)` of the chunks that cover `n` frames, `segment` long and
overlapping by at least `overlap`.

Every chunk is exactly `segment` long (one chunk of `n` when `n <= segment`):
the last one ends at `n`, so it may overlap its neighbour by more than
`overlap`.

```pycon
>>> chunk_bounds(10, segment=4, overlap=1)
[(0, 4), (3, 7), (6, 10)]
>>> chunk_bounds(9, segment=4, overlap=0)
[(0, 4), (4, 8), (5, 9)]
>>> chunk_bounds(3, segment=4, overlap=1)
[(0, 3)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### denote.util.chunked_apply(fn, x, , segment, overlap)

Apply `fn` to overlapping chunks of `x` along its last axis and overlap-add
the results, so `fn` only ever sees `segment` frames at a time.

* **Parameters:**
  * **fn** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`ndarray`], `ndarray`]) – Takes a `(..., m)` chunk of `x` and returns a `(..., m)` array (any
    leading shape, the same for every chunk; `m` frames, as given).
  * **x** (`ndarray`) – Array, typically `(channels, frames)`.
  * **segment** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Chunk length in frames. Every chunk has this length unless `x` is
    shorter (see `chunk_bounds`).
  * **overlap** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Minimum overlap between neighbouring chunks, in frames (0 allowed).
* **Returns:**
  where chunks overlap, a weighted average of their outputs,
  crossfaded linearly over the actual overlap. The output is divided by the
  summed weights, so it is an average even where ramps collide (an overlap
  above half the segment); the ramps alone sum to one wherever exactly two
  chunks overlap and do not collide.
* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

Only the output, a `(frames,)` weight vector and one chunk’s temporaries are
held in memory; the division is done in place.

```pycon
>>> x = np.arange(10.0)[None]
>>> np.allclose(chunked_apply(lambda c: 2 * c, x, segment=4, overlap=1), 2 * x)
True
```

### denote.util.cqt_chroma(y, sr, , hop_length=512)

Constant-Q chroma `(12, frames)` of a mono signal, as librosa returns it.

The one CQT chroma call denote makes, shared by `align` and `get_key`.
Load the audio at `DFLT_AUDIO_SR` first (`load_audio(..., target_sr=...)`):
below about 8.2 kHz librosa refuses the transform.

### denote.util.ensure_file_path(audio, , sr=None)

Ensure audio is available as a file path.

If audio is already a path, return it as a string.
If it’s an array, write to a temporary WAV file and return the path.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### denote.util.load_audio(audio, , sr=None, mono=True, target_sr=None)

Load audio from a file path or validate an existing array.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), `ndarray`]) – File path (str/Path) or numpy array of audio samples.
  * **sr** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Sample rate. Required when audio is an array. Ignored for file paths
    (detected automatically).
  * **mono** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, convert to mono.
  * **target_sr** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – If set, resample to this rate.
* **Return type:**
  [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  Tuple of (audio_array, sample_rate).
* **Raises:**
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If audio is an array and sr is not provided.
  * [**FileNotFoundError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FileNotFoundError) – If audio is a path that doesn’t exist.

### denote.util.peak_normalize(y, , peak=1.0)

`y` scaled so its largest absolute sample is `peak` (a new float32 array).

For models whose voicing decisions depend on input level. All-zero audio is
returned unscaled (as a copy): there is nothing to normalise.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md

# denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker

demucs-mlx worker: HTDemucs on Apple’s MLX, run in the `demucs_mlx` environment.

Loaded standalone by `ps.isolated.Worker` (it imports nothing from denote). The
mix arrives as a `(channels, frames)` float32 `.npy` file at the model’s rate
(44.1 kHz); each requested stem is written back as `<stem>.npy` in the request’s
folder, in the order requested (the model’s order by default).

Normalization is Demucs’s own (`demucs.separate`): the mix minus the mean of its
mono reference, divided by that reference’s std, and undone on the way out; the
mean comes back as `mean / n_sources` per stem, so the stems add up to the mix.
Weights download on first use into demucs-mlx’s cache (`~/.cache/demucs-mlx`, or
`$DEMUCS_MLX_CACHE_DIR`), verified against digests shipped with the package.

### Module Attributes

| [`NORM_EPS`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.NORM_EPS)          | Added to the reference's std, so a silent mix does not divide by zero.              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SINGLE_STEM_MODEL`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.SINGLE_STEM_MODEL) | The model that has one specialist sub-model per stem (single-stem runs are faster). |
| [`SAMPLE_RATE`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.SAMPLE_RATE)       | The rate every demucs model runs at.                                                |

### Functions

| [`load`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.load)(\*\*_)                                  | The worker's state: the separator in use, built on first request.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`separate`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.separate)(state, \*, mix, out_dir, sr[, ...]) | Separate the mix in `mix` (a `.npy` path); write `<stem>.npy` into `out_dir`. |

### denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.NORM_EPS *= 1e-08*

Added to the reference’s std, so a silent mix does not divide by zero.

### denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.SAMPLE_RATE *= 44100*

The rate every demucs model runs at.

### denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.SINGLE_STEM_MODEL *= 'htdemucs_ft'*

The model that has one specialist sub-model per stem (single-stem runs are faster).

### denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.load(\*\*\_)

The worker’s state: the separator in use, built on first request.

demucs-mlx downloads weights with urllib, which verifies TLS against the
interpreter’s OpenSSL defaults; an interpreter built without a CA bundle (some
system and MacPorts Pythons) fails there. certifi’s bundle is used unless
`SSL_CERT_FILE` already names one.

### denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.separate(state, , mix, out_dir, sr, model='htdemucs', sources=None, shifts=1, overlap=0.25, segment=None, seed=None)

Separate the mix in `mix` (a `.npy` path); write `<stem>.npy` into `out_dir`.

  {name: path}, “sr”: rate, “sources”: the model’s stems,
  “model”: model}\`\`; only `sources` (default: all) are written, in that order.


# _autosummary/denote.workers.html.md

# denote.workers

Worker files: model code that runs in a backend’s own environment (`denote.isolated`).

Each `<backend>_worker.py` is loaded standalone by `ps.isolated.Worker` with the
environment’s interpreter, so it imports nothing from denote: it defines
`load(**init) -> state` and operations `op(state, **request) -> dict`.

### Modules

| [`demucs_mlx_worker`](_autosummary/denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker.html.md#module-denote.workers.demucs_mlx_worker)   | demucs-mlx worker: HTDemucs on Apple's MLX, run in the `demucs_mlx` environment.            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`roformer_worker`](_autosummary/denote.workers.roformer_worker.html.md#module-denote.workers.roformer_worker)       | RoFormer worker: audio-separator's RoFormer checkpoints, run in the `roformer` environment. |


# _autosummary/denote.workers.roformer_worker.html.md

# denote.workers.roformer_worker

RoFormer worker: audio-separator’s RoFormer checkpoints, run in the `roformer` environment.

Loaded standalone by `ps.isolated.Worker` (it imports nothing from denote). The
mix arrives as a `(channels, frames)` float32 `.npy` file at 44.1 kHz; it is
written, next to it, as a 32-bit float WAV (audio-separator reads files), separated,
and each stem read back and written as `<stem>.npy` (lower-case stem name) in the
request’s folder. Output WAVs are float too (audio-separator keeps the input’s
subtype), so no level is lost to 16-bit quantization; audio-separator scales a stem
down only if its peak exceeds `normalization_threshold` (1.0 here, its maximum).

Stems come back target first (the checkpoint’s primary stem, e.g. `vocals`), then
the rest in the order audio-separator wrote them (it writes the secondary stem first).
audio-separator writes its outputs into one folder fixed when it is built: a
temporary folder of this worker, emptied after each request and removed at exit.

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`denote` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `opsward`

Run opsward to assess and improve this project’s AI agent setup. Use when the user says ‘opsward’, ‘check my setup’, ‘improve my AI config’, or wants a full audit and remediation.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward).

### `opsward-diagnose`

Diagnose the health of this project’s AI agent setup. Use when the user asks to check, audit, or score the project’s CLAUDE.md, skills, docs, or agent configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-diagnose`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-diagnose).

### `opsward-generate`

Generate missing AI setup artifacts for this project. Use when the user asks to scaffold, create, or bootstrap CLAUDE.md, docs, skills, or agent configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-generate`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-generate).

### `opsward-maintain`

Check documentation and AI setup for staleness, drift, or inconsistency. Use when the user asks to maintain, refresh, or update project docs and AI configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-maintain`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-maintain).

## Subagents

Subagents are Markdown files with a frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`) and a system prompt as the body. Copy one into your project’s `.claude/agents/` (or your agent host’s equivalent) to delegate the task it describes.

### `setup-auditor`

Read-only diagnostic agent that audits the project’s AI setup (CLAUDE.md, skills, docs, rules). Use when you want to check the health of the project’s agent configuration without making changes.

Source: [`.claude/agents/setup-auditor.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/setup-auditor.md).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/denote/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/denote/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`denote.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/denote/denote.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/denote/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
